bullets.title: The Tale of the Unknown Island
bullets.note:
(Saramago) -- This tiny book -- just 51 pages -- can be digested in less than
an hour. It’s a lovely bite-sized piece of fiction. Can you guess my favorite
line? Let me know on Twitter
([@tferriss](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=d7j&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=m&)).
Here’s the description: “Winner of the 1998 Nobel Prize in Literature, this
short, illustrated book begins as a fairy tale with a decidedly political
inflection: an unnamed man waits by the king's door for petitions, a door the
king neglects because he's occupied at the door for favors ("favors being
offered to the king, you understand"). The man's tenacity happily coincides
with the monarch's fear of a popular revolt, which results in the king
begrudgingly granting the man a seaworthy boat with which he can sail to find
"the unknown island." A philosophical discussion about whether such an island
exists or is findable precedes the king's acquiescence, and the reader
understands that the man is a dreamer, with bold imagination and will.”
